architectural_implications.after: A single Model Gateway is the enforcement and observability point for every model request.
architectural_implications.before: Each app/builder independently handles redaction, provider credentials, guardrails, and caching.
architectural_implications.consequence: Compliance becomes auditable and uniform, but the gateway becomes a shared failure domain and latency contributor whose own SLOs are now on the critical path of all AI features.
architectural_implications.observation: PII handling and model safety move from per-application code into a shared gateway.

architectural_implications.after: APIs are crawled and projected into MCPs with standardized auth, discovery, and schema routing.
architectural_implications.before: Engineers manually authenticate and wire each internal API or SaaS tool into each agent.
architectural_implications.consequence: Tool onboarding cost drops, tool supply expands rapidly, and the token/context budget becomes the binding constraint — forcing representation-level optimizations like Omni-MCP and Code Mode.
architectural_implications.observation: Tool integration shifts from hand-written per-tool connectors to auto-projected MCP servers behind a gateway.

architectural_implications.after: Agents read from a bounded graph of typed nodes and edges spanning code, docs, tickets, and data.
architectural_implications.before: Agents issue exploratory queries/searches and assemble context on the fly.
architectural_implications.consequence: Lower token burn and latency plus more predictable outputs, at the cost of a new continuously-maintained index whose coverage gaps become a silent source of wrong answers.
architectural_implications.observation: Context retrieval moves from search-at-inference-time to a maintained typed graph.

architectural_implications.after: Inner/outer automated loops (static analysis, spec-conformance visual diff, staging integration) gate the change first.
architectural_implications.before: Human code review is the primary quality gate for agent and human code.
architectural_implications.consequence: Human review effort can be redirected to design and risk judgment, but validating agents now need their own trust model and can only be as good as the specs (e.g., Figma) they compare against.
architectural_implications.observation: Code validation runs before human review rather than at human review.

architectural_implications.after: DevPods with snapshotted repos and indexes are pre-provisioned regionally, with Mega DevPods for multi-repo agents.
architectural_implications.before: Agents and engineers provision or clone environments on demand, incurring cold starts.
architectural_implications.consequence: Startup drops to seconds and cross-repo edits become feasible, but shared workspaces trade isolation for capability and require cost/eviction policy for idle pods.
architectural_implications.observation: Agent execution environments move from per-developer setup to pre-warmed shared/fleet infrastructure.

article_ideas.angle: Treat gateway adoption as a reliability engineering decision: define the hot-path budget, the fail-open/fail-closed matrix per guard, and the blast radius of a gateway incident across all consuming projects.
article_ideas.audience: Platform and infrastructure engineers building internal AI platforms
article_ideas.based_on: No PII ever leaves Uber's perimeter by default.
article_ideas.thesis: Once PII redaction, guardrails, caching, and cost attribution live in a shared model gateway, compliance stops being a code-review concern and becomes an SLO problem: the gateway becomes a shared failure domain whose latency budget caps every feature built on it, and teams that adopt it without a degraded-mode contract have centralized their risk rather than reduced it.
article_ideas.title: Your AI Gateway Is a Production Service, Not a Policy Checklist

article_ideas.angle: Reframe context bloat as an interface design and platform-ownership question, with representation patterns (aggregated tool surfaces, code-mode exposure) as the primary lever and prompt tuning as the residual.
article_ideas.audience: Agent platform engineers and AI tooling architects
article_ideas.based_on: Omni-MCP and CLI patterns prevent context bloat and reduce fleetwide token consumption by over 40%.
article_ideas.thesis: Fleetwide token consumption is governed primarily by how tools and context are represented to the model, not by prompt phrasing: aggregating tool surfaces or exposing them as code instead of discrete schemas can dominate every other optimization, which means context budget should be owned by the gateway/tooling layer rather than by individual prompt authors.
article_ideas.title: Token Efficiency Is a Tool-Interface Problem, Not a Prompt Problem

article_ideas.angle: Build the counter-metric set that must ship alongside any agentic adoption dashboard, and treat a single systematic agent mistake propagated across millions of auto-migrated lines as the canonical tail risk.
article_ideas.based_on: Over 70% of PRs are now assisted by local or cloud agents.
article_ideas.thesis: Adoption percentage and lines-of-code velocity are throughput metrics that cannot distinguish faster delivery from faster rework; without pairing them against revert rate, post-merge defect rate, and review time, an org can report doubled LOC while quality silently degrades, and the same blind spot applies to automated migration claims at fleet scale.
article_ideas.title: Your Agentic Velocity Metrics Are Measuring the Wrong Thing

article_ideas.angle: Argue that skill authoring conventions are insufficient and map the required package-management controls onto agent skills, including the cost of defaults.
article_ideas.audience: Platform teams running internal agent-skill marketplaces
article_ideas.based_on: A managed marketplace of 2,500+ core and domain-specific agent skills with automated lint checks, reviews, and continuous eval feedback loops.
article_ideas.thesis: Once agents execute skills at fleet scale, skill quality becomes supply-chain management: lint, review, evals, distribution, and default installation are the minimum controls, and persona-based auto-install is in direct tension with token-optimization goals because it inflates the tool surface for every engineer whether or not the skill is relevant.
article_ideas.title: Skill Marketplaces Are Package Registries and Should Be Governed Like One

connections.relationship: Tool representation is reclassified from an integration concern to a primary cost/latency lever, since gateway-level patterns cut fleetwide tokens by over 40%.
Bounded typed retrieval substitutes for unbounded exploration as the mechanism for reducing latency and unpredictable outputs.
Pre-warmed execution environments host the agents that consume gateway-projected tools and graph context, making environment hydration the physical substrate of the software factory.
Skills are gated by lint, review, and continuous eval loops, making the evaluation stack the quality-control boundary for distributed agent capability.
Automated validation is inserted upstream of human review, redefining human review from primary gate to downstream confirmation.

evidence_quotes.text: No PII ever leaves Uber's perimeter by default.
Latency guards and AI Guard run under 100 milliseconds.
Requests are attributed per user, project, and team in real time and data lakes.
Handling over 800 internal projects and over 100 million model requests per day.

core_insights.generalization: Any org running multiple LLM-consuming applications should push PII boundaries, guardrails, caching, and cost attribution into a shared inference gateway rather than an SDK convention, and must then budget for that gateway being in the hot path.
core_insights.insight: Uber routes all LLM traffic through a single Model Gateway that enforces PII redaction, sub-100ms latency/safety guards, LLM caching, and per-user/project/team cost attribution at platform level rather than in each application, at a scale of 800 internal projects and 100M+ model requests per day.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Safety, compliance, and cost accounting become platform invariants enforced once, instead of per-team responsibilities that drift and cannot be audited centrally. It also means every model call in the company transits one control plane, making that plane a critical latency and availability dependency.

evidence_quotes.text: Omni-MCP and CLI patterns prevent context bloat and reduce fleetwide token consumption by over 40%.
Internal APIs and SaaS tools (Slack, Jira, GitHub) are automatically crawled and projected into MCPs.
Eliminates the friction of manual tool authentication and setup while massively optimizing token usage.

core_insights.generalization: Tool exposure format is a first-class optimization dimension: aggregating/compressing tool surfaces (or exposing them as code rather than discrete schemas) can dominate other token-reduction efforts when many tools are available.
core_insights.insight: The MCP Gateway auto-crawls internal APIs and SaaS tools and projects them into MCP servers, and specific tool-representation patterns (Omni-MCP and 'Code Mode') cut fleetwide token consumption by over 40%.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It frames tool/context bloat as a fleet-level cost and latency problem solved by changing how tools are represented to the model, not by writing better prompts. Automatic projection also removes per-team tool auth and setup work.

evidence_quotes.text: A unified context graph capturing 150 unique node/edge types and 40 million entries connecting mobile apps, backend services, data lakes, design docs, Jira issues, and bugs.
Significantly reduces token burn, latency, and unpredictable outcomes compared to unbounded searching.

core_insights.generalization: For large distributed codebases and tool fleets, investing in a maintained typed index may beat retrieval-by-exploration on token cost, latency, and output variance — but shifts cost into index construction and freshness maintenance.
core_insights.insight: Uber built a typed Context Graph (150 node/edge types, 40M entries) spanning services, data lakes, design docs, Jira issues, and bugs, explicitly as a bounded alternative to unbounded agentic search, and claims it reduces token burn, latency, and unpredictable outcomes.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It positions curated, schema-bound retrieval as the reliability mechanism for agent context, implying that 'let the agent explore the repo/graph' is a measurable cost and determinism failure mode rather than a flexibility win.

evidence_quotes.text: DevPods come pre-provisioned with snapshotted repositories and search indexes, reducing startup to seconds.
Mega DevPods provide single common repositories for autonomous multi-repo coding agents.
Pre-provisioned environments across global regions like Oregon, Virginia, Netherlands, São Paulo, and Mumbai.

core_insights.generalization: Agent throughput is often gated by sandbox cold start and repo/index hydration, so snapshotting warmed execution environments is a transferable infrastructure pattern; shared workspaces for multi-repo agents trade isolation for cross-repo editing capability.
core_insights.insight: DevPods are pre-provisioned Kubernetes 'balloon pods' with snapshotted repositories and search indexes that bring agent environment startup down to seconds, deployed regionally; Mega DevPods give multi-repo autonomous agents a single common repository.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It identifies environment provisioning as a dominant latency and reliability cost in agentic coding, addressed by snapshot-based warm starts and shared workspaces rather than by faster models.

evidence_quotes.text: A managed marketplace of 2,500+ core and domain-specific agent skills with automated lint checks, reviews, and continuous eval feedback loops.
Solves skill duplication, sub-par quality, and discovery hassles across repositories.
Drives over 20,000 skill executions per day across the engineering fleet.

core_insights.generalization: Once agents execute skills at fleet scale, skill quality becomes a package-management problem: you need lint, review, evals, distribution, and default installation, not just authoring conventions.
core_insights.insight: Agent Skills are managed as a governed registry — 2,500+ core and domain skills with automated lint checks, reviews, and continuous eval feedback loops, persona-based auto-install, and ~20,000 executions/day — explicitly to eliminate duplication, sub-par quality, and discovery problems across repositories.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It treats prompts/tool bundles as versioned, evaluated, supply-chained artifacts under central quality gates, which is the difference between a skill marketplace and scattered prompt snippets in repos.

evidence_quotes.text: Validation inner and outer loops include static analysis, visual validation against Figma specs, and staging integration.
Self-healing CI and codebase maintenance agents run scheduled cleanups like feature flag removal.
Minion handles cross-repo coding changes for backend and frontend simultaneously.

core_insights.generalization: Autonomous coding pipelines need layered automated validation (static, visual/spec-conformance, integration) if they are to reduce human review load rather than just shift it; the same automation that repairs CI can also weaken checks, so CI-introspection permissions need explicit governance.
core_insights.insight: Validation is split into inner and outer loops that run before human review — static analysis, visual validation against Figma specs, and staging integration — plus self-healing CI and scheduled maintenance agents for tasks like feature-flag removal, so code self-improves prior to human inspection.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It relocates the quality gate upstream of code review, changing the human role from first-pass defect finder to downstream confirmer, and expands the agent's permitted action space into CI and maintenance.

evidence_quotes.text: Moving to monorepos and Bazel established solid foundations for agentic scale.

core_insights.generalization: Before investing in multi-repo coding agents, assess whether build/topology consolidation is the actual prerequisite; agent ROI is partly an artifact of prior engineering-platform decisions.
core_insights.insight: Uber attributes its agentic scale partly to prior infrastructure consolidation: monorepos and Bazel are described as the foundation that made cross-repo agentic work tractable.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It suggests agent effectiveness is downstream of repo/build topology, so teams with fragmented repos may hit structural ceilings on cross-repo agents regardless of model quality.

evidence_quotes.text: No PII ever leaves Uber's perimeter by default.
Latency guards and AI Guard run under 100 milliseconds.
Handling over 800 internal projects and over 100 million model requests per day.
Requests are attributed per user, project, and team in real time and data lakes.

deep_dives.research_question: How do you budget and degrade a shared Model Gateway (PII redaction, guard, cache, attribution) so that one control-plane hop does not become the availability and latency ceiling for every AI feature in the company?
deep_dives.topic: Centralized inference gateway as a critical-path dependency
deep_dives.trigger_insight: No PII ever leaves Uber's perimeter by default.
deep_dives.why: Uber's scale claim (800 projects, 100M+ requests/day) plus a sub-100ms guard budget means the gateway's own SLOs are now the SLOs of all internal AI. Most orgs adopting a gateway decide the policy but never model the failure domain or a degraded-mode contract.

evidence_quotes.text: A unified context graph capturing 150 unique node/edge types and 40 million entries connecting mobile apps, backend services, data lakes, design docs, Jira issues, and bugs.
Significantly reduces token burn, latency, and unpredictable outcomes compared to unbounded searching.

deep_dives.research_question: At what staleness threshold does a 150-node-type, 40M-entry context graph produce confidently wrong context, and are missed-context failures detectable at inference time?
deep_dives.topic: Freshness and coverage failure of a bounded typed context graph
deep_dives.trigger_insight: A unified context graph capturing 150 unique node/edge types and 40 million entries
deep_dives.why: The graph is presented as the reliability mechanism replacing unbounded search, but a curated index converts retrieval errors from visible (agent finds nothing) to silent (agent finds plausible stale edges). Coverage gaps need their own observability before the graph can be trusted as a determinism control.

evidence_quotes.text: Validation inner and outer loops include static analysis, visual validation against Figma specs, and staging integration.
Minion handles cross-repo coding changes for backend and frontend simultaneously.

deep_dives.research_question: What fraction of agent-authored changes pass static analysis, visual-spec validation, and staging integration and still require substantive human correction, and who validates the validators?
deep_dives.topic: Validator escape rate in pre-review automated validation loops
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Validation inner and outer loops include static analysis, visual validation against Figma specs, and staging integration.
deep_dives.why: Moving the quality gate upstream of human review only reduces review load if the automated loops have measured escape rates. Visual validation against Figma specs in particular has a spec that may itself be wrong or outdated, so the loop can systematically bless incorrect output.

evidence_quotes.text: Omni-MCP and CLI patterns prevent context bloat and reduce fleetwide token consumption by over 40%.
Internal APIs and SaaS tools (Slack, Jira, GitHub) are automatically crawled and projected into MCPs.
Auto-installing default skills based on engineer personas.

deep_dives.research_question: Does representation-level compression (Omni-MCP, Code Mode) keep outpacing context growth as tool and skill surfaces expand, or does auto-installed capability re-inflate the prompt?
deep_dives.topic: Tool representation as the dominant token lever
deep_dives.trigger_insight: Omni-MCP and CLI patterns prevent context bloat and reduce fleetwide token consumption by over 40%.
deep_dives.why: A 40% fleetwide reduction from changing how tools are represented reframes context budget as an interface-design problem. But persona-based auto-install and a 2,500-skill marketplace push in the opposite direction, so the net trajectory is an empirical question, not a settled win.

evidence_quotes.text: DevPods come pre-provisioned with snapshotted repositories and search indexes, reducing startup to seconds.
Mega DevPods provide single common repositories for autonomous multi-repo coding agents.
Pre-provisioned environments across global regions like Oregon, Virginia, Netherlands, São Paulo, and Mumbai.

deep_dives.research_question: What is the cost, eviction, and isolation contract for pre-warmed snapshot DevPods and shared Mega DevPods when autonomous multi-repo agents run concurrently across regions?
deep_dives.trigger_insight: DevPods come pre-provisioned with snapshotted repositories and search indexes, reducing startup to seconds.
deep_dives.why: Startup-to-seconds is framed as the throughput unlock, but shared workspaces for multi-repo agents trade repository isolation for cross-repo editing, and idle pre-provisioned pods across five regions create a standing cost and a contention surface that the talk does not quantify.

document.description: One-paragraph summary of Building Blocks for Uber’s Software Factory— Uday Kiran Medisetty & Adam Huda, Uber

key_claims.claim: Over 70% of pull requests at Uber are now assisted by local or cloud agents.
key_claims.evidence: Over 70% of PRs are now assisted by local or cloud agents.
key_claims.verification_question: How is 'assisted' defined and measured, and over what time window and population?

key_claims.claim: Lines of code per engineer more than doubled year over year following agentic AI investment.
key_claims.evidence: Lines of code per engineer have more than doubled year over year.
key_claims.verification_question: Is the increase attributable to agents rather than headcount mix, measurement changes, or generated boilerplate?

key_claims.claim: Omni-MCP and CLI patterns reduced fleetwide token consumption by over 40%.
key_claims.evidence: Omni-MCP and CLI patterns prevent context bloat and reduce fleetwide token consumption by over 40%.
key_claims.verification_question: What is the baseline, scope, and measurement method for the 40% reduction, and does it hold under growing tool/skill counts?

key_claims.claim: The Model Gateway handles over 800 internal projects and over 100 million model requests per day while keeping PII inside Uber's perimeter by default.
key_claims.evidence: Handling over 800 internal projects and over 100 million model requests per day.
key_claims.verification_question: What fraction of traffic bypasses the gateway, and what is the measured false-negative rate of PII redaction?

key_claims.claim: A unified context graph spanning 150 node/edge types and 40 million entries reduces token burn, latency, and unpredictable outcomes versus unbounded searching.
key_claims.evidence: Significantly reduces token burn, latency, and unpredictable outcomes compared to unbounded searching.
key_claims.verification_question: What is the measured delta versus an agentic-search baseline on the same tasks, and how does it degrade with graph staleness?

key_claims.claim: Agent Skills eliminate duplication, sub-par quality, and discovery problems and run over 20,000 executions per day.
key_claims.evidence: Drives over 20,000 skill executions per day across the engineering fleet.
key_claims.verification_question: How is skill quality assessed beyond lint and review, and what is the failure rate of skill executions in production?

key_claims.claim: Minion performs cross-repo backend and frontend changes simultaneously, with validation covering static analysis, visual validation against Figma specs, and staging integration before human review.
key_claims.evidence: Validation inner and outer loops include static analysis, visual validation against Figma specs, and staging integration.
key_claims.verification_question: What proportion of agent-authored changes pass all loops but still require substantive human correction?

key_claims.claim: Self-healing CI and maintenance agents autonomously perform scheduled cleanups such as feature-flag removal.
key_claims.evidence: Self-healing CI and codebase maintenance agents run scheduled cleanups like feature flag removal.
key_claims.verification_question: What guardrails prevent a CI-repairing agent from weakening or disabling checks to achieve a passing build?

open_questions.question: What exactly counts as an 'agent-assisted' PR, and does the 70% adoption correlate with defect, revert, or review-cycle changes rather than only throughput?
open_questions.research_direction: Instrument adoption rate against revert rate, post-merge defect rate, review time, and time-to-first-change per PR to separate velocity from churn.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary reports adoption and LOC velocity but no quality or rework metrics, so faster code volume is indistinguishable from faster rework.

open_questions.question: How is the Context Graph kept fresh and how are coverage gaps detected, given 150 node/edge types across code, docs, tickets, and data lakes?
open_questions.research_direction: Measure agent answer accuracy as a function of graph staleness and measure whether missed-context failures are detectable at inference time.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary states the graph exists and reduces unpredictability, but says nothing about staleness detection, ingestion cadence, or ownership of node types.

open_questions.question: How trustworthy are the 'outer loop' validators, especially visual validation against Figma specs, and what catches cases where the validator itself is wrong or bypassed?
open_questions.research_direction: Build an escape-rate benchmark: sample agent-authored PRs that passed inner/outer loops and measure how many required substantive human correction.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary lists the validation mechanisms but provides no measured precision/recall or escape rate for changes that pass validation and are later found broken.

open_questions.question: How does cost attribution work for multi-agent, multi-model chains where one user action fans out into many gateway requests across agents and sub-tasks?
open_questions.research_direction: Define a trace-correlation ID propagated through agent calls and test whether per-feature unit economics can be reconstructed from gateway telemetry alone.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary claims attribution per user, project, and team but does not describe how lineage is preserved across agent hops.

open_questions.question: Do fleetwide token-consumption patterns (like the claimed 40% reduction) persist as tool counts and skill counts grow, or do auto-installed skills and expanding tool surfaces re-inflate context?
open_questions.research_direction: Track token per task over time while tool/skill counts grow, to see whether representation-level optimizations outpace surface growth.
open_questions.why_unresolved: The summary reports a point-in-time reduction without describing the measurement baseline or how it behaves as the marketplace and gateway surface expand.

project_ideas.based_on: Validation inner and outer loops include static analysis, visual validation against Figma specs, and staging integration.
project_ideas.hypothesis: A measurable fraction (target: quantify, not assume) of agent-authored changes that pass static analysis, spec/visual validation, and staging integration still require substantive human correction, and that escape rate varies systematically by change type (cross-repo, UI-vs-backend, migration).
project_ideas.measurement: Escape rate (share of loop-passing PRs needing substantive correction), stratified by loop coverage and change type; false-pass rate of visual/spec validation against a known-good reference set.
project_ideas.name: Escape-Rate Harness for Agent-Authored PRs
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a pipeline that tags agent-authored PRs with which inner/outer loops they passed, then sample post-merge for substantive human follow-up commits within N days; report escape rate per loop combination and per change category on a fixed task suite.

project_ideas.based_on: Significantly reduces token burn, latency, and unpredictable outcomes compared to unbounded searching.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agent answer accuracy degrades measurably with graph staleness, and missed-context failures from a bounded typed index are not detectable at inference time as errors, producing confident wrong answers rather than visible retrieval failures.
project_ideas.measurement: Accuracy and silent-error rate vs staleness level; token burn and latency delta between bounded-index and unbounded-search retrieval; rate at which the agent flags low confidence when the needed edge is missing.
project_ideas.name: Staleness-Conditioned Context Graph Retrieval Benchmark
project_ideas.poc: Build a small typed context index over a toy multi-repo/service set, introduce controlled staleness (renamed services, deleted tickets, superseded design docs), and run identical agent tasks with a bounded-index retriever versus unbounded search; score for wrongness and for whether the agent signaled uncertainty.

project_ideas.based_on: Requests are attributed per user, project, and team in real time and data lakes.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Per-feature unit economics cannot be reconstructed from gateway telemetry alone unless a trace-correlation ID is propagated across agent hops, so multi-agent fan-out silently misattributes cost to the originating user or project.
project_ideas.measurement: Reconstruction error between gateway-only attribution and ground-truth trace cost per user action; fraction of fan-out requests that lose lineage without explicit propagation.
project_ideas.name: Lineage-Correlated Gateway Cost Attribution
project_ideas.poc: Prototype a gateway shim that stamps a correlation ID at the first request, propagates it through nested agent/sub-agent calls, and attempts to reconstruct per-user-action cost from gateway logs only; compare against an instrumented end-to-end trace as ground truth.

project_ideas.based_on: Omni-MCP and CLI patterns prevent context bloat and reduce fleetwide token consumption by over 40%.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Fleetwide token-per-task does not stay reduced as tool and skill counts grow: persona-based auto-install and marketplace expansion re-inflate the effective tool/context surface, eventually outpacing representation-level compression.
project_ideas.measurement: Tokens per task as a function of installed tool/skill count, with and without representation-level optimization; crossover point where surface growth cancels the compression gain.
project_ideas.name: Context Surface Growth Tracker
project_ideas.poc: Stand up a synthetic agent fleet with adjustable tool counts and auto-installed skill sets, apply representation-level optimizations (aggregated tool surfaces, code-mode exposure) and then grow the surface, tracking tokens per completed task across both regimes.

source.title: Building Blocks for Uber’s Software Factory— Uday Kiran Medisetty & Adam Huda, Uber

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Uday Kiran Medisetty and Adam Huda
  • Channel: AI Engineer
  • Main topic: Agentic AI at Uber scale and building blocks for an AI-native software engineering factory
  • Purpose: To showcase Uber's enterprise-scale architecture and building blocks for an AI-native software engineering factory and demonstrate how agentic workflows operate across the SDLC. Uday Kiran Medisetty and Adam Huda discuss Uber's journey towards a managed software factory powered by agentic AI. Operating across 12 global tech hubs with thousands of engineers, Uber has invested in agentic AI to double line-of-code velocity and automate migration and engineering toil. The talk outlines six core building blocks: Model Gateway, MCP Gateway, DevPods, Agent Skills, Context Graph, and AI Assistant (Cortana), followed by an end-to-end demonstration of how an idea moves from Slack to specs, PRs, self-improvement validation, and codebase maintenance.

Topic Map

Context and Scale of Agentic AI at Uber

  • Explanation: Uday introduces Uber's engineering footprint and how agentic AI investments have drastically improved PR adoption, code volume, and migration toil reduction.
  • Key claims:
    • Over 70% of PRs are now assisted by local or cloud agents.
    • Lines of code per engineer have more than doubled year over year.
    • Over 250 automated migrations have reduced 9 million lines of code automatically.
  • Examples:
    • Moving to monorepos and Bazel established solid foundations for agentic scale.
  • Terminology:
    • Agentic AI
    • Software Factory
    • DevPods
  • Why it matters: Demonstrates that agentic AI can achieve enterprise-wide adoption and dramatically accelerate engineering velocity at massive scale.

Building Block 1: Model Gateway

  • Explanation: Uber's centralized gateway ensuring zero PII leaves perimeter boundaries, bounded latency guards, cost attribution, and LLM caching.
  • Key claims:
    • No PII ever leaves Uber's perimeter by default.
    • Latency guards and AI Guard run under 100 milliseconds.
    • Requests are attributed per user, project, and team in real time and data lakes.
  • Examples:
    • Handling over 800 internal projects and over 100 million model requests per day.
  • Terminology:
    • Model Gateway
    • AI Guard
    • Redact PII
    • Token Optimization
  • Why it matters: Provides enterprise security, strict compliance, cost tracking, and safety guardrails across all internal and external models.

Building Block 2: MCP Gateway

  • Explanation: A centralized gateway for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, standardizing authentication, discovery, schema routing, and token optimization across thousands of internal and SaaS APIs.
  • Key claims:
    • Internal APIs and SaaS tools (Slack, Jira, GitHub) are automatically crawled and projected into MCPs.
    • Omni-MCP and CLI patterns prevent context bloat and reduce fleetwide token consumption by over 40%.
  • Examples:
    • Google, Slack, Jira, and GitHub tools integrated via MCP Gateway.
  • Terminology:
    • MCP Gateway
    • Model Context Protocol
    • Omni-MCP
    • Code Mode
  • Why it matters: Eliminates the friction of manual tool authentication and setup while massively optimizing token usage.

Building Block 3: DevPods

  • Explanation: Pre-provisioned Kubernetes balloon pods providing instant, isolated, globally available development and execution environments for agents and engineers.
  • Key claims:
    • DevPods come pre-provisioned with snapshotted repositories and search indexes, reducing startup to seconds.
    • Mega DevPods provide single common repositories for autonomous multi-repo coding agents.
  • Examples:
    • Pre-provisioned environments across global regions like Oregon, Virginia, Netherlands, São Paulo, and Mumbai.
  • Terminology:
    • DevPods
    • Mega DevPod
    • Kubernetes Balloon Pods
  • Why it matters: Enables fast, secure, isolated, and globally distributed execution environments for autonomous AI agents.

Building Block 4: Agent Skills

  • Explanation: A managed marketplace of 2,500+ core and domain-specific agent skills with automated lint checks, reviews, and continuous eval feedback loops.
  • Key claims:
    • Solves skill duplication, sub-par quality, and discovery hassles across repositories.
    • Drives over 20,000 skill executions per day across the engineering fleet.
  • Examples:
    • Auto-installing default skills based on engineer personas.
  • Terminology:
    • Agent Skills
    • Skill Marketplace
    • Lint Checks
  • Why it matters: Standardizes agent capabilities, eliminates redundant skill development, and ensures baseline quality through automated evals.

Building Block 5: Context Graph

  • Explanation: A unified context graph capturing 150 unique node/edge types and 40 million entries connecting mobile apps, backend services, data lakes, design docs, Jira issues, and bugs.
  • Key claims:
    • Connects scattered systems across Uber to help agents instantly find the correct context.
    • Significantly reduces token burn, latency, and unpredictable outcomes compared to unbounded searching.
  • Examples:
    • Answering mobility trip queries in India by mapping SQL tables and services automatically.
  • Terminology:
    • Context Graph
    • Node and Edge Types
  • Why it matters: Eliminates hallucination and latency caused by fragmented documentation and architecture across dozens of microservices.

Building Block 6: AI Assistant (Cortana)

  • Explanation: An enterprise AI assistant plugged into Slack, CLI, and web surfaces, leveraging skills, MCPs, and the Context Graph to answer questions and run workflows.
  • Key claims:
    • Generates over 300 unique personas and 20,000 sessions per day in the last month.
    • Allows custom skills and custom prompts hooked directly into team Slack channels.
  • Examples:
    • Idea jam on Slack seamlessly transitioning into requirements and specs via Cortana.
  • Terminology:
    • Cortana
